findings.title: Unmapped Graph 404 on move/delete reported Not applied
findings.problem: _graph_status_write routes only the codes in _GRAPH_CODE_MAP (ErrorItemNotFound, ErrorInvalidIdMalformed) to _write_message_not_found. A 404 with any other or no code falls through to the generic `status >= 400` branch and returns WriteRejectedError (Not applied, nothing was changed), even for move/delete after submission where the spec requires not-found of the old id to be Unknown because the first attempt may have succeeded.
findings.impact: After a lost first attempt, a move or delete can be reported as Not applied when it may already have happened, inviting a blind retry or a wrong conclusion about the mailbox state. Reachability of an unmapped-code 404 on this path was not confirmed, so severity is capped at major.
findings.recommendation: In _graph_status_write, before the generic `status >= _HTTP_BAD_REQUEST` fallback, return _write_message_not_found(op, before_mutation) for a 404 on move/delete after submission, so an unmapped-code 404 is Unknown, not Not applied; add tests for an unmapped-code 404 on move and delete.

findings.title: Write input validation strips and normalises model input
findings.problem: security-patterns.md (Untrusted Input Handling) says to parse external input exactly as received and reject what cannot be parsed. validate_recipients strips each address, validate_body_type strips and lowercases, and validate_folder_name and validate_category strip, all before the validity check, so padded values are repaired instead of rejected. validate_message_id checks the stripped value but returns the unstripped one, an inconsistency.
findings.impact: These values drive irreversible send, move, delete and tag actions; the documented fail-closed behaviour is not followed. The checked value is the value used, so no mismatch results today.
findings.recommendation: Validate recipients, folder and category exactly as received and raise InvalidWriteInputError on leading or trailing whitespace instead of stripping; match body_type against the exact allowed values, or document the tolerated normalisation as an explicit exception in security-patterns.md.
